correctness.rationale: For \(q\ge3\), each length-three in-ball intersection splits into a fixed large final-letter class of size \(q(q-1)\), a second class with \(q-1\) elements unless its symbol repeats, and one possible residual singleton. The strict inequality \(q(q-1)>q\) recovers the first symbol; the threshold \(q-1\ge2\) recovers the second; the residual recovers the third. The published prefix-twin bound supplies the matching lower bound. Both separately implemented checkers generated unique nonempty signatures for sizes 3 through 8; finite tests do not prove the infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The exact new assertion is radius-two separation for the endpoint-inequality code at length three when \(q\ge3\). Boutin–Horan Goliber–Pelto already prove the universal size bound, construct this set as a radius-one code, cover radius two at lengths strictly greater than three, and report the binary seven-vertex exception. Neither radius-one identification nor the longer-word radius-two theorem implies the present radius-two length-three claim; explicit closed in-ball decoding closes that gap. Priority remains conditional on unindexed sources.

value.rationale: The integer alphabet family \(q\ge3\) fills the first excluded radius-two word length of the foundational optimality theorem, with a universal lower-bound-matching construction and explicit noncomputational decoding. It identifies a sharp alphabet-size boundary against the known binary seven-vertex exception, directly relevant to minimum sensor placement on shift-register networks. It is a genuine exact infinite-alphabet classification, not a restatement of the earlier radius-one case.
